description: Server-side live detection: when a punch arrives with a device_key already registered to a DIFFERENT employee, treat it as a shared-device event — flag it on the append-only attendance_events audit row and alert admins by bell + email via notifyAdmins. ENFORCEMENT POLICY = DETECT + FLAG + ALERT only (do NOT hard-block), because families and shared office machines are legitimate and a false block would lock a real employee out; the admin can then Block or Delete the device from the Devices tab. This catches sharing live at punch time, complementing the client-side badge from FEAT-002. All new work must be defensive: the detection query must never throw the punch path (which always returns 200 with a verdict).
steps: In supabase/functions/attendance-punch/index.ts, after the existing per-employee device block (the `if (deviceKey) { ... }` section around L160-190 that looks up/inserts attendance_devices for THIS employee), add a defensive cross-employee lookup wrapped in try/catch: when deviceKey is present, query `db.from('attendance_devices').select('employee_id, status').eq('device_key', deviceKey).neq('employee_id', employee.id)`. Capture the first/other owner(s). Store a boolean like `sharedDevice` and the other employee_id(s). Never let a failure here reject or 500 the punch — on any error just skip detection (log nothing or console.warn).

Thread a shared-device signal onto the accepted attendance_events insert. The event is inserted near the end (`await db.from('attendance_events').insert({ ...event, attendance_id, outcome: 'accepted', reason: remote ? 'remote_request' : null })`). When sharedDevice is true, record it in `reason` in a way that composes with the remote case — e.g. set reason to 'shared_device' when not remote, or 'remote_request|shared_device' when both. Keep it a plain lowercase_snake token so the existing Security-tab `.replace(/_/g, ' ')` rendering stays readable. Also set the same flag on the `reject(...)` path's event if a rejected attempt still used a shared key, so sharing is visible even when the punch is rejected for another reason (optional but preferred; keep it defensive).

OPTIONAL hardening (do only if clean): add an idempotent migration supabase/migrations/20260516000008_attendance_events_shared_device.sql adding a nullable column `shared_with_employee_id uuid REFERENCES public.employees(id) ON DELETE SET NULL` to public.attendance_events (ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS), owner-applied. If you add it, set it on the event insert via a BEST-EFFORT separate update wrapped in try/catch so the insert still succeeds when the column does not yet exist (do NOT put the column in the main insert object, or the insert will fail wholesale until the migration is applied — that would break punches). If this cannot be done cleanly and gracefully, SKIP the column and rely on the `reason` token + the admin alert; note the decision in findings.

After the event is recorded on an ACCEPTED punch where sharedDevice is true, alert admins via notifyAdmins(db, {...}) modelled on the existing hr_remote_request block near the end of the file. Use type 'hr_shared_device', a title like `Shared device detected — <employeeName>`, a body naming who punched, the time (use the existing timeIST(nowIso)) and that the device is also registered to another employee, and details rows: Employee (name + code), Device (deviceKey.slice(0,8) + label if available), Also registered to (the other employee's name/code — look it up via a small employees select by id, defensively), Date (today.date), When (timeIST), IP. Set path '/hrms/attendance' and cta 'Open Devices'. Wrap the notify in the same best-effort manner (notifyAdmins already catches internally, but keep the surrounding owner lookups defensive). Fire the alert at most once per punch.

Keep the detection strictly additive: do not change the verdict, do not add a new RejectionReason, and do NOT edit src/lib/attendance-rules.ts or supabase/functions/_shared/attendance-rules.ts (they are byte-identical and test-locked, and no shared pure rule is needed here). Optionally run `npx -y deno check supabase/functions/attendance-punch/index.ts` to sanity-check the edge function compiles under Deno, then delete any deno.lock it creates.

In src/routes/_authenticated/hrms/attendance.tsx Security tab (the events table ~L1360-1520), confirm the new 'shared_device' reason token renders acceptably through the existing `(e.reason ?? '...').replace(/_/g, ' ')` path for accepted/rejected rows. If accepted events are not currently shown with their reason, add a lightweight amber indicator when e.reason contains 'shared_device' so the admin can spot shared-device punches in the Security list too. Keep changes minimal and additive.
Run `npx prettier --write` on every file you created or edited and verify no NEW eslint problems on touched existing files.
acceptance_criteria: attendance-punch/index.ts performs a cross-employee attendance_devices lookup by device_key (excluding the caller's own employee_id) that is fully wrapped so a query failure cannot reject or 500 the punch — the punch still returns its normal 200 verdict.

When a punch uses a device_key registered to a different employee, the attendance_events row records a 'shared_device' signal in `reason` (composed with 'remote_request' when both apply) and admins receive a notifyAdmins alert (type 'hr_shared_device') naming the puncher, the device, and the other owner, linking to /hrms/attendance.

Enforcement is DETECT+FLAG+ALERT only: no hard block is added by default; the verdict for a shared device is unchanged from today. Any optional hard-block mode (not required) would be opt-in via an hr_settings flag, not default-on.
src/lib/attendance-rules.ts and supabase/functions/_shared/attendance-rules.ts are byte-for-byte unchanged (the byte-identical test still passes).

If an attendance_events.shared_with_employee_id migration is added, the event insert still succeeds without it (best-effort update), i.e. punches never break when the migration is unapplied; otherwise the decision to skip the column is recorded in findings.
`./node_modules/.bin/tsc --noEmit`, `bun run test`, and `bun run build` all pass.
findings: IMPLEMENTED server-side live cross-employee shared-device detection in supabase/functions/attendance-punch/index.ts. Files changed: (1) supabase/functions/attendance-punch/index.ts; (2) src/routes/_authenticated/hrms/attendance.tsx (SecurityView accepted-row amber 'shared device' badge); (3) NEW migration supabase/migrations/20260518000003_attendance_events_shared_device.sql. Optional column: ADDED cleanly. Chose next free sequential number 20260518000003 (the feature's suggested 20260516000008 was already taken by hrms_salary_slips; 20260518000002 taken by FEAT-002). It adds nullable shared_with_employee_id uuid REFERENCES public.employees(id) ON DELETE SET NULL via ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS (idempotent, owner-applied). DETECTION BEHAVIOR = DETECT + FLAG + ALERT, NO hard block: after the existing per-employee attendance_devices block, a defensive try/catch query looks up attendance_devices by device_key with .neq('employee_id', employee.id) .limit(1) to find another owner; on hit it sets sharedDevice=true + sharedWithEmployeeId. The accepted attendance_events insert composes reason as 'shared_device', or 'remote_request|shared_device' when both (pipe-joined lowercase_snake tokens so the Security-tab .replace(/_/g,' ') render stays readable). The reject() helper also appends '|shared_device' to its reason so sharing is visible even on rejected attempts. The shared_with_employee_id column is set via a SEPARATE best-effort update (NOT in the main insert object) wrapped in try/catch, so punches NEVER break when the migration is unapplied. Admin alert: notifyAdmins(db,{type:'hr_shared_device', title:`Shared device detected — <name>`, body naming puncher+time+other owner, details rows Employee/Device(key.slice(0,8)+label)/Also registered to/Date/When(timeIST(nowIso))/IP, path '/hrms/attendance', cta 'Open Devices'}), fired at most once per accepted punch, with the OTHER employee looked up defensively via employees select by id. The whole detection+alert path is wrapped so a failure can never reject/500 the punch (handler still returns its normal 200 verdict). WHERE ADMIN SEES IT: bell + email alert (type hr_shared_device) linking to /hrms/attendance Devices tab; plus the Attendance Security tab now shows an amber 'shared device' badge next to 'Accepted' when reason contains shared_device (and the token renders in the rejected-row reason text + CSV export). NOT touched: src/lib/attendance-rules.ts and supabase/functions/_shared/attendance-rules.ts remain byte-identical (byte-identical test still passes); no new RejectionReason added; verdict unchanged. VERIFICATION: ./node_modules/.bin/tsc --noEmit OK; bun run test = 18 files / 289 tests pass; bun run build OK (routeTree.gen.ts unchanged); npx deno check on the edge fn passed (deno.lock removed, not committed); prettier --write applied (index.ts reformatted; .sql has no prettier parser which is expected); eslint on attendance.tsx shows 0 problems before and after (no new errors).
